Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 49
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: European
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Fashion Designer
  trauma_type: Trauma to a loved one
  pcl5: 77

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Future Plans: Making any plans for the future, Suppress Thoughts: try hard not think about the trauma, Mental Distraction: keep mind occupied all the time
  Threat: Negative Emotions: Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame, Sleep Problems: Trouble falling or staying asleep, Physical Reactivity: Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience
  Memory: Guilt on Recall: When I remember the event I feel intense guilt, Overwhelm on Recall: When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop, Partial Clarity: Some moments of the event are extremely clear while others are completely blank

Vignette:
Mark is a 49-year-old European-American fashion designer who has been struggling with intense psychological distress following the traumatic loss of his younger brother in an automobile accident. Mark's relationship with his brother was exceptionally close, and their shared love for fashion had formed a significant part of his identity. The accident occurred about six months ago on a rainy night when Mark’s brother was driving home from a late-night shift at a local design studio. Despite the precautions he took—slowing down, using his lights, and being cautious—the car skidded off the road due to an unexpected patch of black ice. The impact was severe; his brother did not survive. Since then, Mark has found it increasingly difficult to cope with everyday life. He had come to believe that making plans for the future only brought him closer to another potential tragedy. This fear led him to avoid organizing any gatherings or outings, even simple ones like family dinners or weekend getaways. The idea of planning a trip or event filled him with dread and an overwhelming sense of impending doom. His attempts to suppress thoughts about the accident were relentless, but he found himself constantly reliving it in fragments. Sometimes the details were crystal clear—like the sound of screeching tires or his brother’s voice saying goodbye as he left that evening—and at other times, large chunks of memory felt like a complete blank. Each time these memories resurfaced, Mark felt an intense wave of guilt and horror wash over him. He was certain that if only he had insisted on driving his brother home instead of letting him go alone, the accident might have been avoided. To cope with these overwhelming feelings, Mark kept himself occupied at all times. He would work late into the night, often staying up until the early hours of the morning to avoid sleep and the potential nightmares that came with it. His mind was a constant whirlwind of ideas for new designs and projects, each one serving as a temporary distraction from his inner turmoil. His relationship with his wife had also suffered due to these avoidance behaviors. She felt increasingly isolated as Mark withdrew into his work and kept their interactions at arm's length. When they would talk about the future or make plans together, he often became visibly upset and agitated, leading to more arguments and emotional distance between them. Despite his efforts to distract himself, strong physical reactions still plagued him whenever something reminded him of the accident. The sound of rain on a windshield, the sight of black ice on the road, or even the smell of leather seats in a car could trigger intense panic attacks and flashbacks that left him feeling physically drained and emotionally exhausted. Mark had come to realize that his life was becoming increasingly unmanageable. He had reached out for help only after a recent incident where he became so overwhelmed at work that he broke down in front of his colleagues, unable to cope with the constant anxiety and fear. What frightened him most was the idea of losing control completely and being unable to function as a designer or a husband. In seeking therapy, Mark expressed hope that he could find ways to process his grief and trauma without it consuming every aspect of his life. He wanted to regain some sense of normalcy and be able to make plans for the future again—plans that didn’t feel like a death sentence waiting to happen.
